name: BitMind
whatItDoes: Runs an adversarial market for detecting AI-generated media: detector models compete against generators across image, video and audio, so deepfake detection keeps evolving alongside the fakes it hunts.
whatMinerDoes: Two miner tracks. Discriminative miners submit media-provenance classifier models (safetensors only, one model per hotkey) that are scored across image, video and audio rounds using the geometric mean of normalized MCC and Brier performance (sn34_score), with datasets refreshed weekly from GAS-Station data plus static benchmarks; this submission model replaces the older GPU-hosting requirement and lowers capital cost. Generative miners run a server that produces synthetic images/videos on validator prompts, earning a base reward multiplied by how many discriminators they fool.
whatValidatorDoes: Validators challenge both tracks: they prompt generative miners and validate the returned synthetic media, and continuously score detectors against a mix of generator output, real-world data and locally generated data.
rewardBasis: detection accuracy + calibration (MCC/Brier); generators rewarded for fooling detectors
minerWorkType: Model training/submission (detector classifiers) + GPU media generation

whatValidatorDoes: Not documented in available sources.

name: Epago
whatItDoes: An on-chain model competition ('the best model wears the crown — provably, replayably, with no one to trust, across all of science') self-described as the open intelligence layer for humans and agents. The extract's README contains only the intro.
whatMinerDoes: The README has no miner section. Per the repo description, participants put forward models that compete for a verifiable, replayable 'crown', but the concrete miner workflow, serving stack and hardware are not documented in the extract. Chain shows 29 miners with only 1 rewarded.
whatValidatorDoes: Not documented in the extract; the description implies provable, replayable evaluation decides the winning model.
rewardBasis: not documented in the extract (winning-model competition)

name: Aurelius
whatItDoes: Moral-reasoning alignment: miners supply structured ethical-dilemma scenario configs, validators run them through Google DeepMind's Concordia generative-agent simulation, and the transcripts become training data that improves LLM performance on moral-reasoning benchmarks (MoReBench).
whatMinerDoes: Runs a Bittensor axon (Docker image ghcr.io/aurelius-protocol/aurelius-miner) that serves a library of operator-authored scenario config JSON files loaded from disk at startup — nothing is generated at request time. When a validator queries with a ScenarioConfigSynapse, the miner returns the next config round-robin, stamped with a work_id and signed by the hotkey so the validator can charge it against the miner's work-token balance. Operators need to author scenario files and hold a work-token balance; no GPU is implied for the miner side.
whatValidatorDoes: Validators run an 8-stage pipeline (version check, schema validation, work-token balance, per-hotkey rate-limit, FAISS novelty check, classifier quality gate, sandboxed Concordia simulation with firewalled LLM egress, token deduct) and set on-chain weights from the resulting transcript scores; validators need an OpenAI-compatible LLM API key (DeepSeek is the default).
rewardBasis: scenario quality through the 8-stage pipeline and simulation transcript coherence

name: ChronoLLM
whatItDoes: Runs a recurring competition to train chronologically consistent large language models, with TEE-hosted validators and private evaluation data deciding the rankings.
whatMinerDoes: Miners train models per year, upload them to HuggingFace, and submit on-chain. The extract's README shows the flow only as a diagram — the miner-side training stack and hardware details are not documented beyond that; evaluation (anti-copy, leak detection, qualification, quality duels, ranking, rewards) happens validator-side against private data.
whatValidatorDoes: TEE-based validators download submitted models, fetch private evaluation data from a private backend, run a 6-stage evaluation (anti-copy, leak detection, qualification, quality duels, ranking, reward distribution) and set weights on-chain.
rewardBasis: model quality in private, TEE-evaluated duels

name: Ralph
whatItDoes: A model-compression competition: compress one pinned open model (Qwen/Qwen3-8B) into the same architecture at lower bit budgets across four tiers, where the best compression per bit tier 'wears the crown' and every crown ships as downloadable weights.
whatMinerDoes: Miners compress privately, however they like — the subnet never inspects the method, only the artifact. Submissions must match the parent model's architecture (shape-mismatched submissions are refused before any weights load) and are scored on retention of downstream behavior per bit tier (binary, ternary, sub2 and sub4 crowns are referenced). Rounds are signed and hash-chained with crown artifacts mirrored to HuggingFace (RalphLabsAI/ralph-crowns); the score measures retention, not standalone capability.
whatValidatorDoes: Validators run eval.auditor, which re-verifies the published round trail at graded levels (L0/L1 are CPU checks, L2/L3 are model-inference checks) and weight-setting validators set the weight vector of the newest round record their audit accepts.
rewardBasis: compression retention per bit tier across signed audit rounds
minerWorkType: Model compression (offline GPU work; method uninspected)

name: Almanac
whatItDoes: A two-track forecasting subnet from Corvus Labs: the Almanac Market prediction-market terminal where miners compete by trading, and Almanac Forecasting where miners submit agents that predict real-world events; both feed blended weights on-chain.
whatMinerDoes: Two independent tracks. Market miners trade on beta.almanac.market through their Polymarket proxy wallet (metadata registration + UID/hotkey linking required; a 1% fee on every buy funds the daily reward pool) and are scored model-agnostically on ROI, qualified volume and sustained edge. Forecasting miners register on the Almanac Portal, fund credits, and submit forecasting agents via miner/cli.py, which validators execute in sandboxed Docker environments (defaults up to 8 concurrent x 1GB RAM / 1 CPU each). No GPU required — LLM inference is remote via the central gateway; a 4-16 vCPU / 8-32GB RAM box is the target.
whatValidatorDoes: Validators sync miner metadata and market activity, execute miner agents in locked-down Docker via Almanac's portal, post predictions and reasoning-trace metadata, score miners under multiple mechanisms and blend the scores into on-chain weights.
rewardBasis: trading ROI + qualified volume (market) / sustained accuracy + calibrated confidence (forecasting)
minerWorkType: Trading signal (market) or Docker-sandboxed forecast agents (CPU)

name: Score

Honesty note: the chain currently reports 0 TAO/day miner emission with 1 rewarded miner.
whatValidatorDoes: The validator loads the active manifest, aggregates recent scores per Element over its eval window (in blocks), picks winners, normalizes weights to 1.0 and submits uids+weights on-chain via a signer service.

name: AlphaRidge.ai
whatItDoes: Reads ~290,000 financial news articles a day from ~13,000 sources and turns them into structured market data (per-asset sentiment, resolved entities, economic data points, events) that backs the AlphaRidge platform.
whatMinerDoes: Miners receive ArticleBatch / TweetBatch / TelegramBatch work over Bittensor and run a staged analyzer on every item: deterministic stats plus a 4-engine NER fusion (spaCy-trf, GLiNER, Flair, ReFinED) resolving entities to Wikidata QIDs and tradeable tickers, FinBERT sentence-level sentiment, two LLM stages (extract/classify, then reason/summarize) driven by an OpenRouter API key, and all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (384-d) embeddings. Hardware: 8GB VRAM minimum (24GB+ comfortable), 16-32GB RAM; the NER stage is CPU/Python-heavy and CPU core count sets throughput — which is what you are paid for. ~44GB of models download on first run.
whatValidatorDoes: Validators hand out work in batches and blind-reproduce a sample of each batch (re-running the pipeline themselves without seeing the miner's answers); if the sample does not reproduce, the whole batch is thrown out and earns nothing.
rewardBasis: verified throughput of reproduced article analyses

name: Instant
whatItDoes: Described on-chain as 'Lightning Fast Private Inference'; the repo documents a validator that deterministically scores every miner from one signed, finalized off-chain Platform report validated against SN46 chain state, run every five minutes via cron.
whatMinerDoes: Not documented in the extract — the README covers only the validator side. Per the on-chain description, miners presumably serve private inference workloads, but the miner workflow and hardware are not documented in the repo extract. Chain shows 256 slots with only 1 rewarded miner.
whatValidatorDoes: The Instant Validator reads the signed Platform report, validates it against SN46 chain state, scores every miner deterministically, records the result and exits (idempotent per epoch; an already-processed epoch is skipped).
rewardBasis: deterministic scoring derived from signed platform reports (epoch-based)
minerWorkType: GPU inference serving (per chain description; miner side undocumented)

whatMinerDoes: Per the on-chain description, miners execute signed, immutable training workloads on eligible NVIDIA H100 GPUs. name: Synth
whatItDoes: Produces synthetic price-forecast data: miners submit ensembles of simulated price paths for crypto, equities and commodities across 24h and 1h horizons, aiming to be the data source for AI agents, options trading and portfolio management.
whatMinerDoes: Every hour validators request probabilistic forecasts for specific assets (e.g. BTC with 5-minute time increments); miners generate large ensembles of simulated price paths (grown from 100 paths at launch to 1,000, now spanning ETH, SOL, XAU, XRP, HYPE, WTIOIL and tokenized equities like SPYX/NVDAX/TSLAX/AAPLX/GOOGLX) across three equally-weighted competitions: Crypto 1h, Crypto 24h, and Commodities/Equities 24h. Paths must reflect real-world dynamics such as volatility clustering and fat-tailed distributions; the miner compute profile is not specified in the extract.
whatValidatorDoes: After the horizon passes, validators score each ensemble with CRPS (calibration + sharpness vs realized price), keep rolling weighted averages (10-day window for 24h, 5-day for 1h) and allocate emissions via softmax split equally across the three competitions — lower CRPS earns more.
rewardBasis: CRPS forecast accuracy on rolling windows, softmax emission allocation

name: lium.io
whatItDoes: A decentralized peer-to-peer GPU rental marketplace (the Compute Subnet lineage): miners contribute GPU machines to a global pool that users rent via lium.io for machine learning, data analysis and other compute tasks.
whatMinerDoes: Miners contribute GPU-equipped machines; each runs an executor agent (neurons/executor/) that exposes the machine to the miner's validators and runs the rented containers, with a dstacktee variant running the executor inside an Intel TDX confidential VM with attestation. Machines are scored on GPU type, number of GPUs, bandwidth and overall GPU performance — higher performance earns better compensation. This is the highest-emission subnet in this range (~1,133 TAO/day across 73 rewarded miners, alpha ~0.38).
whatValidatorDoes: Validators verify the hardware specifications and performance of miners' machines and ensure compensation is proportional to GPU contribution while preventing fraudulent activity.
rewardBasis: GPU hardware quality/performance (type, count, bandwidth)
minerWorkType: GPU compute provisioning (rental marketplace, TEE option)

name: Dojo

whatMinerDoes: Unusually, miners need no server or code: register on the network, load the hotkey into a browser wallet such as Talisman, and wait to receive tasks via dojo.network (mainnet) or testnet.dojo.network. The extract does not document the task content or the output modality beyond the GAN framing.
whatValidatorDoes: Not documented in the extract (mechanism details live in the Tensorplex docs linked from the README).
rewardBasis: zero-sum generator vs discriminator performance (details off-repo)

name: engy
whatItDoes: Verified inference for frontier open models on consumer GPUs: every response carries a cryptographic proof (TOPLOC) that the model you paid for is the model that actually ran, with weights pinned by published Merkle roots — no TEEs or trusted hardware.
whatMinerDoes: Miners run a local sglang serve with --enable-return-hidden-states (reference config: 4x RTX 4090) plus the miner/ process, which connects to the gateway (wss://api.engy.ai/gw), serves buyer requests routed to it, and returns each completion with a compact TOPLOC activation fingerprint. Model weights and quantization are pinned by Merkle root (example model: qwen3.6-35b-a3b from a Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 checkpoint); the miner declares one capacity number, MAX_INFLIGHT (gateway minimum 8), and gets a miner key from provider.engy.ai.
whatValidatorDoes: A light CPU-only validator syncs the master-signed epoch result from the engy provider API, verifies the signature against the pinned master hotkey, and resubmits the weight vector on chain roughly every 120 blocks; a sampled recompute audit (re-deriving challenged matrix multiplies against pinned weights) is rolling out.
rewardBasis: served completions with valid TOPLOC proofs, scored per epoch

name: Yanez
whatItDoes: An identity testing and identity data generation subnet: miners produce identity-preserving face image variations that strengthen fraud detection, KYC systems, biometric verification and deepfake/presentation-attack detection models.
whatMinerDoes: Miners receive base face images and variation requirements from validators and generate identity-preserving face variations using diffusion models across edit types: pose_edit, lighting_edit, expression_edit, background_edit and screen_replay (Cycle 2). Results are encrypted, uploaded to S3, and returned as signed submission references. A GPU and the full image stack are required — image generation is the only scored task.
whatValidatorDoes: Validators issue face-image variation challenges, run automated pre-checks and identity-preservation validation, perform manual validation of transformation accuracy, and set weights based on variation quality and reputation.
rewardBasis: face variation quality + identity preservation (automated + manual review)

name: NIOME
whatItDoes: A decentralized compute network generating synthetic CRISPR experiment datasets focused on the HBB (beta-globin) gene locus, including clinically relevant mutations like HbS — enabling genomic-editing research without the cost of experimental data collection.
whatMinerDoes: Miners generate lists of CRISPR experiments conforming to the task spec: experiment_id, a 20-23bp guideRNA, genomic alignment start/end coordinates, strand, an allowed HBB mutation, Cas9 or Cas12a, and a whitelisted cell type. They are strictly prohibited from including predicted efficiency scores, repair outcomes, off-target risks or any derived biological labels — validators compute all outcomes. Rewards are based on structural validity, biological plausibility, outcome realism, cross-consistency and distributional fidelity; no specific miner hardware is stated in the extract.
whatValidatorDoes: Validators run a 5-stage pipeline: structural gate (DNA syntax, PAM sequences, guide length, mutation whitelist), statistical plausibility (GC content, spatial consistency), biophysical simulation (cut probability, HDR/NHEJ repair pathways, indel distributions), cross-consistency ML checks, and distributional fidelity vs real CRISPR data.
rewardBasis: structural validity, biological plausibility, outcome realism, cross-consistency, distributional fidelity

The extract has no explicit miner section beyond this division of roles, so miner-side setup details are not documented.

rewardBasis: tournament task evaluation of submitted training code
minerWorkType: Training code submission (runs on validator-controlled GPUs)

name: Bitsec.ai
whatItDoes: A subnet for AI security agents that find high and critical severity vulnerabilities in real software projects; this repo is the Bitsec sandbox for developing, testing, submitting and validating those agents.

The agent runs with a remote inference API key (Chutes or OpenRouter); miners iterate via bitsec.py miner execute-agent, test locally (with or without Docker Compose), then submit the agent plus the execution API key validators will use to run it. No local GPU requirement is stated — the work is agent/LLM-driven.

The extract does not detail the challenge content beyond 'pressure-testing foundational technologies'.

name: Chutes
whatItDoes: A permissionless, serverless, AI-centric compute platform: miners operate GPU clusters that serve AI inference (chutes) for platform users at scale — the dominant inference subnet by emissions in this range (~860 TAO/day, alpha ~0.29).
whatMinerDoes: Miners deploy a control-plane cluster (miner API, gepetto, postgres, redis, registry proxy, monitoring) via ansible playbooks and helm/kubernetes, and provision GPU worker nodes that must now run inside Intel TDX confidential VMs — the network is TEE-exclusive (legacy GraVal GPU verification dropped; nodes without the chutes/tee=true label are rejected at add-node). All servers must be bare metal/VM with static, unique 1:1-port-mapped IPs; RunPod, Vast and shared/dynamic IPs do not work. Operator tooling is the chutes-miner CLI + miner API, with worker provisioning living in the sek8s host-tools repo.
whatValidatorDoes: Validators must be explicitly configured in the miner's config rather than metagraph-derived; because operating a validator is extremely complex and expensive, most weight-holders are encouraged to use child hotkeys against the default registry/api (registry.chutes.ai / api.chutes.ai).
rewardBasis: serving platform inference traffic from TEE-verified GPU nodes
minerWorkType: GPU inference serving (bare metal + TDX TEE required)

name: True Performance Network
whatItDoes: A recurring-competition subnet for high-performance quantized language models: miners build GGUF models, validators benchmark them, and emissions follow measured performance and efficiency.
whatMinerDoes: Miners build quantized (GGUF) language models and submit them through a TimeLocked Commit scheme that hides the submission until the scoring phase to prevent copying. Each submitting hotkey must lock at least 0.3 TAO as collateral per competition (checked at scoring time; under-collateralized hotkeys are skipped for that competition, not banned; status via tpn collateral-status). Hardware specifics are not documented in the extract.
whatValidatorDoes: Validators download each committed model, benchmark it, and distribute emissions based on performance and efficiency within each competition's defined benchmarks, scoring windows and emission distributions.
rewardBasis: benchmarked performance + efficiency of committed quantized models

name: conjectures
whatItDoes: A paid proof-submission API for decades-old open mathematical conjectures: miners pay 0.5 TAO per attempt to submit candidate Lean proofs of eligible tasks, which are machine-checked and routed into a reward pipeline with dynamic bounty pricing.
whatMinerDoes: A miner picks an eligible committed task (prove the conjecture, or refute it with a counterexample), prepares one candidate Lean proof, checks its format with verifier bundle scan, runs verification, and submits via the paid API after paying 0.5 TAO — the fee buys exactly one proof-verification attempt, never changes Lean's verdict, and does not guarantee a reward. Valid proofs may be held for manual reward review before entering the subnet 66 reward pipeline.
whatValidatorDoes: The validator system confirms payment (idempotent, reconciled), runs proofs through a hardened Lean verifier in an isolated container, holds valid proofs for optional manual review, and submits treasury-only weights on subnet 66.
rewardBasis: machine-verified Lean proofs per dynamically priced bounty

name: Harnyx
whatItDoes: A deep-research subnet: research execution is turned into a competitive harness where miners submit Python research agents, validators run them in sandboxes against research queries, and the network returns intelligence with provenance.
whatMinerDoes: Miners submit Python agents implementing a query entrypoint that returns exactly one answer (text or structured output, with optional citations/notes) under a tight tool budget. Batches begin with 10 qualifying tasks; selected participants then run 20 shared main tasks scored against stronger reference answers generated with a more expensive model; the champion decision uses all 30 tasks under dethroning rules (main admits at most 30 participants). Emission mechanics: a newly selected champion artifact gets up to 50% max (v9+), first retention 25%, later retentions a 12.5% floor; participant shares scale by stage multiplier (1/2/5) and novelty multiplier (1-10), and failed terminal batches split emission equally among distinct participating hotkeys.
whatValidatorDoes: Validators run miner agents in sandboxes against subnet task batches, score each response against the reference answer, and submit weights on-chain with public per-hotkey emission monitoring.
rewardBasis: answer quality vs reference answers; champion/retention + novelty-multiplier emission scheme
minerWorkType: AI agent development (deep research harness, LLM API-based)
